detailed_rationale:
Bata India is the domestic arm of the 130-year-old Bata footwear group (parent holds 50%, operates 5,300+ stores globally), running an extensive Indian retail and wholesale footwear network. The quant data's near-zero three-year (0.6%) and one-year (0.8%) revenue growth is corroborated by screener's quarterly trend: sales have oscillated in a narrow Rs.800-945cr band for two years with no discernible growth trend. More concerning is the trajectory of returns - ROCE has fallen from 25% in FY2020 to 13% in FY2026, a structural six-year decline, and net profit has nearly halved from Rs.263cr (Mar 2024) to Rs.134cr (Mar 2026).

This pattern - flat top-line, halving profit, and steadily eroding capital returns - is consistent with a mature, brand-led retailer facing intensifying competition from newer D2C and online footwear brands, alongside structurally higher rental and labour costs eating into what used to be a very high-return retail model. There is no leverage or governance red flag here (promoter holding stable at 50.16%, no pledge or related-party concerns noted), and the dividend payout remains healthy (72.9%), but none of that offsets a business that is simply not growing while its multiple remains rich.

Reverse-DCF: at 54-65x trailing earnings (quant PE 65.1, screener PE 54.2), the market continues to pay a premium multiple for a business whose returns on capital have been cut nearly in half over six years and whose revenue has not grown in two years. This is a case where the fundamentals have already deteriorated materially while the multiple has not caught up - the stock is down 40% over one year and 26% over three, but starting valuation was high enough that even after the de-rating it remains expensive relative to current earnings power.
recommendation_rationale: The quant model scores this Sell on both the 3-year (38.1) and 1-year (38.4) composites with no divergence between the two - a consistent signal, not a borderline one. Our own read (stagnant growth, ROCE nearly halved over six years, still-rich multiple, no offsetting balance-sheet cheapness) aligns fully with that quant signal, so we confirm rather than rescue.
summary: Bata India's footwear business has been essentially flat on revenue for two years while profit has nearly halved and returns on capital have fallen from 25% to 13% over the past six years, reflecting rising competition from newer footwear brands and higher operating costs. Despite a roughly 30-40% stock price decline, the shares still trade at a rich 54-65 times trailing earnings for a business that is not growing. We recommend continuing to treat this as a Sell.
positive_para: Bata carries strong brand equity and a wide retail footprint backed by a global 130-year-old parent, has kept a healthy dividend payout (72.9%) even through the slowdown, and has actually improved working-capital efficiency (working-capital days down from 25 to 17). Promoter ownership is stable with no signs of distress-driven selling, and the stock has already de-rated meaningfully (down 40% over one year), which reduces some of the downside risk relative to where it traded previously.
negative_para: Revenue has been essentially flat for two years and profit has nearly halved (Rs.263cr to Rs.134cr) over the same period, while ROCE has fallen from 25% to 13% over six years - a genuine structural erosion in the quality of the business, not a one-quarter blip. At 54-65x trailing earnings, the stock has not yet re-rated down to reflect that erosion, leaving limited margin of safety if competitive pressure from newer footwear brands continues.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A mid-50s to mid-60s P/E implies the market still expects Bata to defend or rebuild its historically strong (20-25%) returns on capital. The six-year decline to 13% ROCE alongside two years of flat revenue suggests the business has structurally re-rated to a lower-return retailer, meaning the current multiple has not fully caught up with the deterioration in underlying quality.
